tools.name: av_hash_lookup
tools.description: CrushAV file reputation, no key needed: look up up to 100 SHA-256 file hashes. For each hash something is known about, returns `knownMalicious` (the source listing it as malware), `malwareName`, `trust` (0-100: how sure CIRCL hashlookup is that this is a published, known-good file from NSRL or a maj

tools.name: reputation_lookup
tools.description: Look up an IP address or a domain against the ThreatCrush community threat database (what every linked ThreatCrush daemon blocked). Returns `listed` (the corroboration bar: independent reporters agree), a 0-100 `score`, severity, reports, reporters, rules and country; a domain is answered from its A

tools.name: reputation_bulk
tools.description: Look up many IPs or domains at once (up to 100 with a free key, 1,000 with Reputation Pro). Results come back in request order; each counts against the daily allowance.

tools.name: redeem_credit_code
tools.description: Redeem a ThreatCrush credit code (CR-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX) into the signed-in account's credit balance (1 credit = $1.00). Needs the account's session token (`threatcrush login`), not a tc_agent_ key: agent keys belong to a team, not a person.

tools.name: list_invites
tools.description: The signed-in account's invites: how many are left of 3, who joined, and whether the bonus credits were paid. Session token only.

tools.name: create_invite
tools.description: Create one invite link (each account has 3, single use, 30 days). When a new account joins on it and confirms its email, both get bonus credits. Session token only.

tools.name: findings_list
tools.description: Your org's tracked findings from threatcrush scan, pentest and ai-scan (deduped across runs, with a triage status). Default: open + acknowledged. Session token or tc_agent_ key.

tools.name: findings_get
tools.description: One tracked finding with its details (code snippet, remediation, evidence), property and history.

tools.name: findings_triage
tools.description: Set the status and/or note of up to 500 findings: acknowledged, fixed, false_positive, ignored or open. fixed is reopened by a later run that still sees it; false_positive and ignored never are. Needs write.

tools.name: incidents_list
tools.description: Your org's incidents: what `threatcrush investigate --raise`, the daemon (critical detections) and people raised to humans. Filter by host and explicit since timestamp; only teams you can see. Session token or tc_agent_ key.

tools.name: incidents_get
tools.description: One incident: linked forensic evidence, recent events from the same observed source IP on its server, block history for that IP, saved AI assessment, multi-person assignees, fix and test progress, work history, recorded resolution/operator, findings, timeline, notes and who was paged.

tools.name: incidents_update
tools.description: Update fix work performed by your assigned agent or human: set multiple assignees, fix status, PR URL, test status and evidence, verification or blocker, and/or add a note. ThreatCrush catalogs the incident and does not execute remediation. Closing requires status fixed with passing tests and verifi

tools.name: incidents_raise
tools.description: Raise an incident report (report_version 1: title, severity, source, dedupe_key, summary, verdict, findings, timeline, recommendations, optional team_id/server_id). The same dedupe_key while open updates it; a new incident pages the team by SMS and email once. Reports that contain anything shaped li

tools.name: webhooks_list
tools.description: Your org's webhook endpoints (signed Standard Webhooks deliveries, retried for about three days) and the events ThreatCrush emits: detection.created, findings.raised, reputation.changed. Endpoints behind a Webhook alert destination follow your alert rules; the others get every event they subscribe t

tools.name: webhooks_create
tools.description: Add a webhook endpoint (public https URL). Returns the endpoint and its signing secret (whsec_…), shown once.

tools.name: webhooks_update
tools.description: Change a webhook endpoint's url, events, description, or switch it on/off (on again clears its failure count).

tools.name: webhooks_delete
tools.description: Remove a webhook endpoint and its delivery log.

tools.name: webhooks_test
tools.description: Send a signed webhook.test event to one endpoint now and say how it went.

tools.name: webhooks_rotate_secret
tools.description: Replace an endpoint's signing secret; the old one stops working at once. Returns the new secret.

tools.name: webhooks_deliveries
tools.description: Recent webhook deliveries (status, attempts, last HTTP status/error, payload), for one endpoint or all.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_invite, incidents_raise · Private data: av_hash_lookup, reputation_lookup, redeem_credit_code, list_invites, create_invite, findings_list, incidents_list, incidents_raise, webhooks_list, webhooks_create, webhooks_rotate_secret · Public sink: av_hash_lookup, create_invite, incidents_raise, webhooks_list, webhooks_create, webhooks_update, webhooks_delete, webhooks_test, webhooks_deliveries · Destructive: findings_triage, incidents_update, webhooks_delete.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_invite, incidents_raise · Private data: av_hash_lookup, reputation_lookup, redeem_credit_code, list_invites, create_invite, findings_list, incidents_list, incidents_raise, webhooks_list, webhooks_create, webhooks_rotate_secret · Public sink: av_hash_lookup, create_invite, incidents_raise, webhooks_list, webhooks_create, webhooks_update, webhooks_delete, webhooks_test, webhooks_deliveries · Destructive: findings_triage, incidents_update, webhooks_delete

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
